item.content:encoded:
The containment protocols specify "criminal" background/behavior. The Foundation, not being a government or even a true "society", can only set protocols and rules not "laws". Thus while what she did was against the rules, it isn't considered "criminal" so isn't anything that "Judgment" would seem to particularly care about…if it even cares about "human law" at all.

As a side note, it also seems that "Judgment" may also have a different set of criteria as to what the definition of "criminal" is compared to the general consensus of human society/governments, as many of the Foundation's standard operating procedures would be criminal under most, if not all, of the legal systems of the world's nations. Outright theft of objects, kidnapping, brainwashing (which is pretty much what amnesiacs amount to) etc…not to mention that the use of D-class as "lab rats" in testing that often ends with them dying in horrific ways, which could fall under such various charges as murder, human right violations, or simply violation of the "cruel and unusual punishment" statues of many countries. After all, unwilling human experimentation, even upon death row prisoners, is a crime in and of itself in most places. As most, if not all, Foundation staff know about such things going on, that would make them accomplices by most countries legal systems, or at the very least accomplices after the fact. There is also the fact that pretty much everyone with a driver's license has, at one time or another, purposefully ignored the posted speed limit…which, though a minor misdemeanor, still qualifies as a criminal offense by human law.

Putting all that together, the only assumption that one can really come to is that "Judgement" is working off a set of "laws" that have little or nothing to actually do with human law systems, but simply have some common points (Much like how most cultures, even though having absolutely no contact with each other at any point, came up with the "murder is a crime" idea.). As the only thing shown is that "Judgment" has said it is the final arbitrator of "guilt" and punishment within it's sphere of influence we have no way of knowing what the criteria it uses to determine that "guilt" is, other then in reference to our own legal system…which, so far, seems to be working.

It would be interesting for someone to ask though…

item.content:encoded: I'm a bit conflicted on this one. The image and the general idea are great, and I'd love to see them get expanded upon. However, the whole "Safe/Euclid/Keter" thing is pretty goofy, and the way the information in the article is presented is also weird- I know that part of the appeal probably comes from piecing together what actually caused the skip to come into existence, but a few more hints and clues would've been nice. The tone could also use some work, as other people have pointed out. But most importantly, I think that Judgment should've been fleshed out more, either through an Interview Log or some other addendum. They're the most interesting aspect of the article, but the reader gets to see very little of them. I'm neutral voting, but that may change.

item.content:encoded:
Glad to know the author is still around. +1 for sure.

So, I was wondering why they wouldn't want to get some of the scips back by "feeding" Judgment, but I guess that's part of it, right? Judgment hasn't given them the option to choose where the executions get "assigned", so-to-speak, so SCP-ohcrapwereallgonnadie could be released first instead of the harmless one they want to get out that produces sugar and happiness for everyone? =P

And actually… How do Safe Class objects get let out? If it's not a scip capable of murdering someone, how can Judgment use it in an "execution" in order to secure the item's release? (That's how it kills, right?) Now that I've started thinking about all this, that's the only hangup I'm having with it. The 56 statues represent every SCP item that was in ACS-03 (plus one for Judgment itself) when the nuke was set off, right? So Safe through Keter are all represented? They don't just represent the dangerous items, yeah?

It may be very difficult to add in, but if possible to pull off, I know I'd like to see Judgment explain the reasoning for containing the Safe things, and how they're supposed to get released from "custody" if they can't be used to carry out its sentences on the "guilty". Seeing as how Judgment has thus far been relatively cooperative and forthcoming with non-guilty people, I think it would be fairly reasonable for a researcher to ask about that.

item.content:encoded:
It seems to me that the general premise is as follows:

+ show block
– hide block

The site previous held 55 SCPs.
An incident(s) led to necessary detonation of the on site nuclear warhead.
In the blast crater is an amphitheater housing 56 statues.
Judgement - this is what 296 is, as well as the 56th statue - decides if entering personel are "guilty."
Guilty parties are executed by means of one of the old SCPs previously held on site.
Once the SCP imprisoned in the statue has been used in enough executions it will be released.
One SCP previously held on site, presumably the one that required previous destruction of Site is imprisoned in a statue and the Foundation doesn't want to release it and don't know what order it will be used in so they don't let more criminals in to be executed.

Or at least that's how I interpreted it. Anyway, hope that helped.

On the other hand, taken on its own, this is a well-written article that provides an intriguing glimpse into what could happen when a bunch of SCPs contained at a Site get sorta fused as a result of detonating on-site nukes.
